color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Knowledge travels on an orphan branch, harness-state
No shared history with the product. The product tree stays clean
A .harness folder on the developer's branch is opt-in
One YAML file per entity, sorted keys, stable IDs
Written after each published revision, debounced
SQLite itself is not committed. CRDTs are not in v1:
they do not resolve two different cutoff times

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Exported: decisions, quotes, research, architecture, contracts,
plans, visible examples, receipts, feature progress
Held-back examples: yes, encrypted with a project key in the vault
Transcripts: opt-in. Secrets and tokens: never. Re-enter them per machine
Leases, paths and process IDs: no. Usage: a summary per feature
Checkpoint refs: optional, so a parked task can resume elsewhere
History: append-only segments of change sets, versions and edges
Incremental export with git fast-import. Op IDs and event numbers stay local

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Opening the folder finds harness-state
Import revision N rebuilds state.db
Running tasks become parked. Resume from pushed checkpoints,
or restart from the brief. Local backups help only if the folder was saved

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Settings, Export project. The same files, as a zip

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
lease.yaml beside manifest.yaml: device ID, holder, epoch,
heartbeat, revision. Compared with writer_epoch on open
The writer refreshes it when it pushes
Another device: open read-only, or take over
Take over increments the epoch. The old device's next push is rejected,
it parks, and it becomes read-only
A stale heartbeat can be taken without a warning
Two devices offline: the second push loses and stays read-only.
Its local checkpoints can be offered to the driver
A force-pushed state branch: ask which revision to keep. Never overwrite

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Interview, plan, build, land. One driver in v1

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Browse and comment. Comments sync as entities
Their Git edits are treated as the developer's edits

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The driver hands over, or a viewer takes over. Epoch increments

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One daemon. Each project has its own coordinator and database
The broker owns plan windows, concurrency and machine slots
It grants a project a short lease: N sessions and a share, for 10 minutes
The project spends that grant inside its own database
Unused grants return. The broker never revokes a running slot
Two projects together cannot pass the plan share the developer allowed

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: One slot per connection is always reserved. It gets the next slot

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Weighted fair share. A third project starts as background or batch
until it is focused. The switcher shows each project's share

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Public repo: state push is off by default, opt-in per project
Private repo: ask once on the first push
Held-back checks stay encrypted either way
Lost project key: regenerate held-back cases for unfinished tasks
Finished tasks keep their receipts

svg.text: Moving a project, and sharing one plan across projects
